transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-27 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sam Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (Lyra CTO), Maya Patel (Lyra Lead Eng), Ravi Singh (Lyra SRE)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming behavior, key request params, retry and reconnect patterns. Agreed to run a short pilot; customer asked about latency guarantees, VPC/private deployment options, and encryption/KMS.

Topics:
- Hosted chat API walkthrough (stream handshake, streaming reconnects)
- Parameter tuning: max tokens, temperature, top_p, stop sequences, prompt shaping
- Retry strategies, idempotency, and backoff guidance
- Observability via Console and Optimize recommendations (batching / cache hints)

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Sam Ortiz: okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining us today, this is Sam from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Priya our solutions eng.
00:07 Priya Nair: hi all, Priya here, SE, i'll do the live sandbox demo and then we can go into q&a and the retry patterns.
00:13 Daniel Cho: hey Sam, thanks, and thanks Priya, i got Maya and Ravi on, we wanted to see how streaming behaves for our realtime assist use case.
00:22 Maya Patel: yes our main constraint is low tail latency and predictable cost, we get flurries of traffic around product launches.
00:30 Ravi Singh: and from infra we need to understand VPC/private options and audit logs for compliance.
00:35 Sam Ortiz: totally, we'll cover hosted first then talk about Dedicated / Private options. we'll start with a quick demo of a streaming chat request and show what to tune.
00:44 Priya Nair: alright pulling up the console, i'm in the sandbox workspace we provision for lyra — link to sandbox: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/lyra (demo link).
00:56 Priya Nair: i'm going to send a chat generation request, you'll see the server does a streaming handshake; note that the initial "event" includes meta (model, token-budget). sometimes the auto-transcript shows it as hand-shake, or hand wave, heh.
01:12 Maya Patel: when you say handshake, is that the long-poll or a websocket under the hood?
01:17 Priya Nair: good q — hosted API supports HTTP streaming (chunked transfer) and websockets for heavier realtime; default SDK uses streaming chunks over HTTP. the handshake is basically the HTTP response starting then tokens stream.
01:28 Daniel Cho: how do we handle partial failure mid-stream? what if connection dies at token 200 of 800?
01:34 Priya Nair: there are three approaches — client-side resume where you reconnect and request the remaining prefix (you'll need to send the prefix in prompt and set the offset), server-side approach using KV cache prefixing, and last-resort full retry. we recommend idempotent request keys and strong backoff.
01:50 Sam Ortiz: i'll add that the SDKs expose an "idempotency_key" header — use that so retries won't double-run billing-sensitive jobs. also we expose resume tokens for some models, though that is model-specific.
02:03 Ravi Singh: resume tokens, is that like a session key that references cached KV on your side? any PII concerns?
02:10 Priya Nair: it's basically a pointer to a cached prefix in our KV cache. important to note — for hosted we store cache either encrypted at rest; if you opt into private deployment you can use your KMS/HSM or customer-managed cache.
02:24 Maya Patel: okay, can you show param tuning? our devs are confused about temperature vs top_p vs max_tokens for concise assistant answers.
02:31 Priya Nair: sure — watch the live req: i'm setting max_tokens=150, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, stop=["

User:"] — the effect: lower temp reduces randomness; top_p is nucleus sampling so together you can control diversity.
02:46 Priya Nair: also show streaming chunk-size: smaller max_chunk_bytes reduces perceived latency but increases total compute cost slightly.
02:55 Daniel Cho: is chunk size configurable? and does it affect token billing?
:58 Priya Nair: yes configurable client-side, billing still per token generated. chunking doesn't change tokens, just how we parcel them.
03:05 Sam Ortiz: a common tradeoff: if you prioritize p50 latency tune for smaller chunks and lower batch windows; if you prioritize cost tune batching and longer windows.
03:17 Maya Patel: are there auto-suggestions? said Redwood Optimize could recommend batching/quantization?
03:22 Priya Nair: exactly — Optimize will analyze your traffic and recommend quantization, model variant (int8), and batching policy. we'll show a small example later.
03:31 Daniel Cho: can hosted meet our SLA needs? we need sub-300ms p50 for short prompts, and 95th under 1s ideally.
03:38 Sam Ortiz: for small prompts we often hit p50 ~120–200ms on c5/gpu-backed endpoints for the curated small models. for larger contexts p95 will depend on model and token length. Dedicated capacity is better when you need consistent 95th tail SLAs.
03:54 Ravi Singh: so Dedicated gives us predictable throughput. what's the commitment model? monthly reserve?
03:59 Sam Ortiz: yes committed monthly or annual reserved GPU pools; you can also configure burst capacity for spiky traffic.
04:06 Maya Patel: what about compliance — SOC2, AD integration, SSO?
04:10 Sam Ortiz: we have SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and audit logs exposed in the Console. i'll attach the security pack after the call.
04:20 Daniel Cho: KMS integration for hosted — can we use our own KMS?
04:24 Priya Nair: for hosted, we manage encryption keys by default; customer-managed KMS is available with Private deployment or Dedicated with enterprise package. hosted can do envelope encryption for customer data if requested.
04:36 Maya Patel: that helps. show us an example of a retry/backoff pattern you recommend for streaming clients.
04:41 Priya Nair: sure — typical pattern: exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 attempts, use idempotency_key on every retry; if you get partial stream, attempt resume with prefix + verification checksum. if resume not available fall back to full retry.
04:59 Priya Nair: for example code (pseudo):
05:03 Priya Nair: - send request with idempotency_key
05:06 Priya Nair: - on network drop: wait base * 2^attempt + jitter, reconnect and ask server for resume if present
05:12 Maya Patel: do you enforce rate limits per token or per request? our bot does lots of short requests per user.
05:18 Sam Ortiz: rate limits are both per second requests and per token. Console shows your quota and current rate; you can request higher rate for pilot.
05:26 Daniel Cho: curious about cost controls — can we set per-route budgets?
05:29 Sam Ortiz: yes console supports per-route budgets and alerts. also Optimize suggests batching to reduce token cost per inference for multi-turn scenarios.
05:37 Ravi Singh: any pitfalls with prompt caching we should be aware of? we have lots of repeating prefixes.
05:42 Priya Nair: prefix (KV) caching is great for repeated system or context prompts. watch out for cache staleness and don't cache PII; you can set TTLs and invalidate. cached items are encrypted at rest.
05:55 Maya Patel: show me the Console traces for a slow request — how do we debug a p95 spike?
06:00 Priya Nair: toggling to traces: you can filter by model, route, and token counts. we show per-token timing, compilation overhead, and kernel selection notes. sometimes the spike is kernel JIT on first cold sequence.
06:15 Daniel Cho: kernel selection notes, interesting — can we pin models to particular runtime optimizations?
06:20 Priya Nair: you can pin model variants, and pick quantization profile. Redwood's runtime chooses kernels by default but you can override on Dedicated.
06:30 Sam Ortiz: quick aside: a lot of customers start on hosted, validate with a pilot, then move to Dedicated if they hit predictable high concurrency.
06:38 Maya Patel: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? we want to go from POC to pilot in ~4 weeks.
06:44 Sam Ortiz: that is feasible — typical pilot: week 0-1 sandbox integration, week 2 run bench and quality evals, week 3 tweak params and Optimize recommendations, week 4 smoke and sign off.
06:53 Daniel Cho: any gotchas with idempotency and billing on retries? we've seen double billing with other vendors.
06:58 Priya Nair: if you supply idempotency_key we dedupe on server and avoid double billing for successful runs; partial streams require careful client semantics — we recommend logging the last-acked token index and include that in resume requests.
07:14 Maya Patel: can you demo a failing stream and a resume?
07:18 Priya Nair: yes i'll throttle my network (mimic drop) — sending request now... (noise) okay dropped, reconnecting... we reconnected with resume and server sent remaining tokens. the console shows an event labeled "partial_stream_resume" — sometimes auto-transcription shows it as "partial stream re-zoom" haha.
07:39 Ravi Singh: nice. what's the visibility in logs? can we pull the raw stream events to our SIEM?
07:44 Sam Ortiz: yes audit logs are exportable to S3/Cloud and you can stream to Splunk/Datadog. event types include request_start, request_end, partial_resume, model_fallback, and quota_alert.
07:58 Daniel Cho: model_fallback? explain.
08:01 Priya Nair: model fallback is when smart routing routes to a lower-cost compatible variant during capacity pressure. there's a per-route policy to allow or block fallbacks.
08:12 Maya Patel: and drift in quality with fallback — how do we monitor?
08:16 Sam Ortiz: Console's quality monitor ties eval suites to traffic and will alert when fallback causes regressions on key prompts. you can set thresholds and auto-fallback rules.
08:28 Daniel Cho: for the pilot we need to run a small eval set, can Priya help us add our prompts?
08:33 Priya Nair: absolutely, we'll import your prompt set into the eval tool and run it during the bench. Priya: please email the CSV.
08:39 Maya Patel: will do. also curious about embeddings — are they separate billing and throughput?
08:44 Sam Ortiz: embeddings are separate units; throughput depends on model and we have dedicated embedding endpoints for high-throughput use.
08:51 Ravi Singh: okay, can we talk briefly about cost-saving knobs like quantization?
08:54 Priya Nair: quantization to int8 can reduce runtime cost ~2-3x with some small quality delta; Optimize will recommend when a workload is safe to quantize using held-out prompts.
09:06 Daniel Cho: do you provide per-tenant isolation on hosted? we have multi-tenant product.
09:11 Sam Ortiz: hosted is logically isolated per project; dedicated offers stronger isolation; private deployment is single-tenant. we can map routes to projects and enforce quotas.
09:21 Maya Patel: any compliance docs we can circulate?
09:23 Sam Ortiz: i'll share SOC2, pen-test summary, encryption notes, and KMS options.
09:28 Priya Nair: quick demo — switching to the console Optimize tab: here's a recommended batching policy for high-frequency small prompts — it suggests 40ms batch window and cache prefixes for 60% repeated prefix hit rate.
09:45 Daniel Cho: 40ms sounds low, will that add latency?
09:48 Priya Nair: it's a tradeoff — 40ms batching slightly increases p50 for single requests but reduces unit cost massively. we can A/B test that in pilot.
09:58 Maya Patel: can we control per-endpoint batching?
10:01 Priya Nair: yes per-route config in the Console; you can also set per-route fallback policies and model pins.
10:08 Sam Ortiz: quick note on quotas — if you hit quota we'll 429, and the response has retry-after. SDKs will surface that.
10:16 Ravi Singh: last technical: do you support token streaming compression or binary frames to reduce bandwidth?
10:22 Priya Nair: not out of the box for HTTP chunking; for websockets we can support binary frames. usually token sizes are small but if bandwidth is a concern we can explore bespoke websocket approach.
10:35 Daniel Cho: ok good. timeline, next steps recap?
10:38 Sam Ortiz: we'll: 1) Priya runs bench with Lyra payloads, 2) Sam sends security pack and pricing, 3) Priya shares retry sample code and console runbook, 4) Lyra to share eval prompts and target pilot dates.
10:52 Maya Patel: thanks, expecting the security docs and pricing this week if possible.
10:56 Sam Ortiz: yes will do.
11:00 Priya Nair: any final questions about streaming params or resume?
11:04 Daniel Cho: one thing — you mentioned resume tokens being model-specific; does that affect which models we can choose?
11:10 Priya Nair: some open models support resume with prefix pointers more naturally; our curated variants expose resume where safe. if resume is critical we can help pick variants that support it.
11:22 Ravi Singh: if we decide to pilot, what's the minimal setup to start?
11:25 Sam Ortiz: just a sandbox API key, a route, and your small eval set; we'll give a sample client and the runbook. Usually 2 engineers can integrate in a couple days.
11:35 Maya Patel: perfect, we'll aim to start integration first week of Aug.
11:38 Sam Ortiz: great — thanks all. we'll follow up with the attachments and schedule the bench next week.
11:46 Daniel Cho: appreciate it, bye.
11:48 Maya Patel: thanks bye.

Post-meeting notes:
- Customer prioritized: low tail latency and per-route cost controls.
- Risk: may require Dedicated if p95 can't be guaranteed on hosted for larger context.
- Pilot success criteria: p50 < 250ms for short prompts, p95 < 1s for typical sessions, <10% cost increase from baseline.
